'''Preda V. Mihăilescu''' ({{IPA|ro|mihə.iˈlesku}}) (born 23 May 1955) is a Romanian mathematician, best known for his proof of the [[Catalan's conjecture]], first proposed in 1844.

==Biography==
Born in [[Bucharest]],<ref name="stewart">Stewart 2013</ref> he is the brother of [[Vintilă Mihăilescu]].

After leaving Romania in 1973, he settled in [[Switzerland]].<ref name="stewart" />  He studied mathematics and computer science in [[Zürich]], receiving a PhD from [[ETH Zürich]] in 1997.<ref>Campbell 2002</ref> His PhD thesis, titled ''Cyclotomy of rings and primality testing'',<ref>Mihăilescu 1997.</ref> was written under the direction of [[Erwin Engeler]] and [[Hendrik Lenstra]].

For several years, he did research at the [[University of Paderborn]], Germany. Since 2005, he has held a professorship at the [[University of Göttingen]].

==Major research==
In 2002, Mihăilescu proved [[Catalan's conjecture]].<ref>Metsänkylä 2004.</ref><ref>Schoof 2008.</ref><ref>Bilu et al. 2014.</ref> This number-theoretical conjecture, formulated by the French and Belgian mathematician [[Eugène Charles Catalan]] in 1844, had stood unresolved for 158 years. Mihăilescu's proof appeared in ''[[Crelle's Journal]]'' in 2004.
